args.question: Hi - I'm Black and White has way more discs than me right now (34 to 20), only 10 empty squares left. My legal moves are g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. Which one gives me the best shot at winning by the end?

parts.content:
Best move: **b7**.

Key reason: it plays on the lower-left edge without immediately giving White easy access to the **a8 corner**, and it helps limit White’s replies in the final 10 squares. In this endgame, the deciding feature is **corner/control access**, not how many discs you flip right now.
Okay, that makes sense - don't just chase flips, watch out for the corners. Let's go with b7.

args.question: White just took a8 corner. Now my options are g2, b6, a7, c8. There's still a1 and h1 corners open too. Which move should I make now?

parts.content:
Play **c8**.

The deciding feature here is **endgame mobility plus corner access**: **c8** is the quiet edge move that doesn’t open either **a1** or **h1**, and it keeps White’s replies more constrained. The other moves let White more easily cash in the remaining corner/edge squares.

Yes — the least bad/best shot is **a7**.

Reason: **a7 is next to a corner White already has (a8), so it can’t “give away” that corner anymore**, while **g2 is dangerous because it sits diagonally next to the still-open h1 corner**. Also, **a7 grabs edge discs and helps reduce White’s clean corner access in the last few moves**.

args.question: Looking back, that c8 move you had me play really seemed to backfire - white jumped from 32 to 36 right after. Was that actually a mistake, or was it still the best option I had at the time?
Also I'm curious why white couldn't play at g2 right after I took h1 - can you explain in plain terms why that square became a dead end for them?

parts.content: That White jump **doesn’t by itself prove c8 was a mistake**—late flips are often temporary, and the deciding feature is usually **who gets the last stable corners/edges and whether you can force passes**. Looking at the final board, Black lost **30–34**, so the line didn’t quite salvage it; I’d call **c8 a reasonable “mobility/corner-access” try**, but I can’t honestly verify it was definitively best without the exact board from that turn.

Yes: **g2 was illegal for White because Othello requires a sandwich, not just touching Black discs**. After you took **h1**, the nearby lines from **g2** toward **h1/h2/g1** ran into the edge with Black discs but **no White disc on the far side**, so White couldn’t flip anything that way. The deciding feature was **bracketing**: if a move doesn’t flip at least one disc in a straight line, it’s a dead square for that player.

That clears it up a bit - so it wasn't a guaranteed mistake, more like a gamble that didn't quite pay off, and that h1 corner grab worked because White just had no way to sandwich anything at g2 after that. Makes more sense now. Well, 30-34 isn't a win, but I get why it played out the way it did. Thanks for walking me through it.
